subject: Committed GPU capacity: term options, ramp schedule, and start window (QuantaFlow)
messages:
From: Olly Grant <olly@quantaflow.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: QuantaFlow Procurement <procurement@quantaflow.com>
Date: 2025-11-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Committed GPU capacity options for inference (QuantaFlow)

Hi Laura,

We’re kicking off procurement for committed GPU capacity to support our production inference workloads. We have a rough 12-month forecast attached but need clarity on how you price reserved commits across 12/24/36 month terms, what discounts look like by tier, and how flexible the ramp/start window can be. Two specific asks from our side:

- Can you provide per-GPU unit pricing and effective unit price after discount for typical pool sizes (16, 64, 128 GPUs) for each term option?
- What throughput guarantees / SLOs do you offer (p50/p95 latency targets and burst capacity behavior) and are those tied to a minimum sustained usage?

Also: how do early-termination credits and pause/slow-start options work — we may have a delayed project start (target Jan 2026) and want to understand financial exposure.

Attached: QF_usage_forecast.csv (monthly token/throughput estimate)

Would like to get a commercial sketch this week so we can align with our finance team. Happy to set a call — what’s your availability?

Thanks,
Olly
Olly Grant
Head of Procurement | QuantaFlow
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olly Grant <olly@quantaflow.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-11-11T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Committed GPU capacity options for inference (QuantaFlow)

Hi Olly — thanks for the forecast and clear asks. Attaching a short template that outlines the Reserved Commit construct we typically use plus a quick example pricing matrix. High level answers up front:

- We price on a per-GPU-month committed basis. Effective unit price drops with longer terms and larger pools; typical list-to-effective discounts range from ~10% (12m small pools) up to ~32% (36m large pools) depending on burst and SLA add-ons.
- Throughput guarantees: we offer tiered SLOs. Base SLA includes burst pooling and automatic regional fallback; add-on SLA guarantees p95 latency and an availability-backed throughput floor expressed as tokens/sec per-GPU.
- Start windows and pauses: we provide a 90-day flexible start for contracts signed with a defined ramp schedule; earlier termination has a stepped credit schedule (we can share worked examples).

I’ve attached: redwood_reserved_commit_template_v1.pdf (contract skeleton) and a short worked example PDF. To avoid back-and-forth, Karthik can propose a technical ramp that ties your forecast to GPU sizing and throughput. Marcus will include a commercial sketch with exact discount breakpoints.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call Thursday 11/13 10:00–10:30 PST to align on target pool size and start date. Does that work?

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales, Dedicated | Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood_reserved_commit_template_v1.pdf (pdf)]

Laura —
Thanks. Two clarifications before the call:

1) Early termination: can you share an example for a 24-month commit that starts 2026-01-04 but where we might only need 50% utilization for the first 3 months? How are credits applied and is there a minimum repayment?

2) Sizing: in our forecast we show bursts that require short-term spikes to ~1.8x sustained throughput. Does the reserved pool support burst above committed capacity automatically or do we need to purchase separate burst credits?

I’ve re-attached the forecast (QF_usage_forecast.csv) with a highlighted ramp quarter. Can you confirm the call for 11/13?

Olly
[attachment: QF_usage_forecast.csv (csv)]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olly Grant <olly@quantaflow.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-11-13T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Committed GPU capacity options for inference (QuantaFlow)

Hi Olly — quick technical note from the ramp side (happy to cover on the call):

- GPU pool sizing: based on the CSV, your 64-GPU configuration looks sensible as a starting point for your baseline. For the burst profile (~1.8x) we recommend keeping a 10–20% headroom in the pool and enabling regional burst policies; that allows short spikes to be absorbed without provisioning an entire additional reserve.
- Throughput guarantees: our Reserved Commit includes a baseline tokens/sec per-GPU floor. If you need strict p95 latency guarantees under burst, we offer a SLA add-on that reserves micro-shards for critical traffic. Without the add-on, burst is handled via automatic queue prioritization and best-effort capacity from spare regional pools.
- Ramp schedule: suggested phased ramp — Month 0: 25% baseline (validation), Month 1–2: 60% (pilot), Month 3: 100% (production). If you sign now and set start = 2026-01-04, we can keep the 90-day flex start for 1x onramp; unused committed months in the first quarter get credited at 50% of list and can be reallocated within the contract.

Happy to run a short perf test against a 16-GPU slice if you want concrete latency curves before committing.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olly Grant <olly@quantaflow.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-11-15T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: Commercial sketch — QuantaFlow RF-2025-QF-3782

Olly — following up with the commercial options we discussed on the call. High level (per-GPU-month committed):

Option A — 12 months, pool 64 GPUs: list $2,800 / GPU-mo, effective after discount $2,520 (10% discount).
Option B — 24 months, pool 64 GPUs: list $2,800 / GPU-mo, effective after discount $2,016 (28% discount + 2 months credit applied prorata).
Option C — 36 months, pool 128 GPUs: list $2,600 / GPU-mo, effective after discount $1,772 (32% discount + onboarding credits).

Key commercial terms:
- Flexible start window: sign by 2025-12-15 to lock start window of 2026-01-04 with 90-day rate protection.
- Early termination: stepped credit schedule — >18 months served = 70% credit remaining, 12–18 months = 50% credit, <12 months = 20% credit.
- Burst policy: base plan includes automated regional burst (no extra purchase for short spikes up to 1.5x sustained). Strict p95 SLA add-on priced at +12% of committed spend.

I’ve attached a formal proposal (proposal_QF_RF-2025-QF-3782.pdf) that includes a worked example for the 24-month option showing monthly invoices and amortized onboarding credit. If those numbers look good I can push to DocuSign and include a standard PO template.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890

Thanks — Marcus
